title: Prefect lost, duplicate hint and partial A1 finish: the committed release and cursor are the only authority
annotator: claude-sonnet-5.5 worker, hand annotation on 2026-10-24 (hand-reading by a language model; no human review; no program produced any expected value)
independence_statement: Scenarios are written as short stories with hand-chosen release numbers and cursor values. Expected outcomes follow the written rules: the scheduler is external, cursor progress means durable admission, A1 releases are atomic with authority, and hints are not evidence. No scheduler, A1 store or A2 code was run or imported.

cases.title: Authority advanced but release missing is a defect, never silently skipped

cases.rationale: Handoff spec H6 forbids this A1 state, so A1 can never present it as a release. A2 consumes only committed releases and creates none. What A2 reports about the violated invariant is not decided by the cited rules; see T0-09-N08.

cases.title: PROPOSED POLICY: authority advanced but release missing is surfaced, never silently ignored

input.visible_to_a2: authority revision and release table of the saved A1 catalog

cases.rationale: PROPOSED POLICY requiring owner sign-off. H6 and H18 do not say how A2 reacts to a violated A1 invariant. H18 covers a bad entry that exists. It does not cover a missing entry. The oracle proposes a visible failure that does not advance the cursor.
